_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#1 — the WALL element's GP pair is read differently on triangles and on quadrilaterals, and neither spelling is a safe default. Eight arms of one self-contained 2D deck (inline nodes, unit square, left edge clamped, right edge line-Neumann), run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: WALL TRI3 and TRI6 with 'GP 3 0' run to 'processor 0 finished normally'; the same two elements with 'GP 3 3' abort with 'Unknown number of Gauss points for tri element' from w1/4C_w1_input.cpp line 223. The mirror image also holds and is the part that makes a single default impossible: WALL QUAD4 with 'GP 3 3' runs, while WALL QUAD4 with 'GP 3 0' aborts with a DIFFERENT message, 'Insufficient number of Gauss points' — TRI_AND_QUAD_SHARE_A_MESSAGE=no, so an agent cannot grep for one string and cover both. EAS is the second triangle restriction and is 4-node-only; 'EAS full' names the cell type it was handed, so TRI3 gives 'eas-technology not implemented for tri3 elements' and TRI6 gives '... tri6 elements' (the entry quotes only the tri3 wording, which is right for TRI3 and not for TRI6).
expect_in_output: Unknown number of Gauss points for tri element
eas-technology not implemented for tri3 elements
eas-technology not implemented for tri6 elements

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the TRI3 arm: give the triangle its legal '<n> 0' rule back. That arm then runs, the tri Gauss-point abort disappears and EXIT_TRI3_GP33 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.

remove the pathology from the QUAD4 arm: give the quad its legal '<n> <n>' rule back. 'Insufficient number of Gauss points' then never appears and EXIT_QUAD4_GP30 becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the TRI3 EAS arm: switch EAS off. The eas-technology throw disappears and EXIT_TRI3_EAS becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
